# Intake Brief: Enemy Best Practices — Audio Instructions

**Headline:** Add a dedicated, consolidated "Audio Best Practices" section to `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` covering spawn, shoot (fire), and explode (destruction) sounds — including when to call each function, scope rules (entity vs scene level), and per-enemy audio decisions.

---

## Problem Statement

The enemy best practices document (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`) currently scatters audio-related guidance across a few checklist items and a table. There is no clear, consolidated set of instructions telling developers and AI agents **when to play audio, which function to call, and at what scope** for spawn, shoot, and explode events. This makes it easy to forget audio or wire it incorrectly when creating new enemy gym scenes.

## Users

- **AI agents and developers** creating new enemy gym scenes (e.g., E4 Phaser, E5 Swarm, Boss)
- **Code reviewers** verifying that audio is correctly implemented in new scenes

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new `## Audio Best Practices` section exists in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, clearly organized by event type (spawn, shoot, explode/destruction).
2. The spawn section specifies: which function to call (`playSpawnSound()`), when (during entity creation in the spawn loop), and scope (base class owns this — §3.1 checklist item 5 confirms base handles it).
3. The shoot section specifies: which functions to call per enemy type (e.g., `playScoutAdvanceCue()` + `playScoutFireSound()` for Scout, `playTankAdvanceCue()` + `playTankFireSound()` for Tank, `playSwarmBurstSound()` for Swarm), when to call each (advance cue timing, fire sound timing), scope rules (entity-level vs scene-level), and the no-gap pattern for Tank.
4. The explode/destruction section specifies: which function to call (`playDestructionSound()`), when (during entity destruction), and the critical ownership rule (base class owns destruction sound — entities must NOT call `playDestructionSound()` to avoid double-playing).
5. The section references `src/audio/effects.ts` as the source of all audio functions and links to GDD §7.3 for the audio event catalog.

## Constraints

- Do not change the audio implementation code (`src/audio/effects.ts`) — this is documentation only.
- Align with existing conventions already in the document (e.g., the destruction sound ownership rule already mentioned in §3.1 item 7).
- Keep the section concise and scannable — it should be a quick reference.

## Existing State

- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` has audio mentioned in §3.1 checklist items 5 and 7, and in the §3.2 audio table.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` contains all audio functions: `playSpawnSound()`, `playDestructionSound()`, `playTankAdvanceCue()`, `playTankFireSound()`, `playScoutAdvanceCue()`, `playScoutFireSound()`, `playSwarmBurstSound()`, and power-up / weapon sounds.
- GDD §7.3 defines the audio event catalog and advance telegraphing requirements.
- The document already covers audio-related gotchas (e.g., no double-playing destruction sounds).

## Desired Change

Add a dedicated, well-organized `## Audio Best Practices` section to the enemy design document that consolidates all audio instructions into one scannable reference, covering spawn, shoot, and explode events with clear function names, timing, and scope rules.

## Key Files

- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — The document to update
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Source of all audio functions (reference only)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — Audio event catalog (reference only)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Operator may expect implementation changes (audio wiring in code) — scope is documentation only.
- **Assumption:** The operator wants documentation only, not code changes. If implementation changes are also needed, a new work item should be created.
- **Assumption:** The existing structure of the enemy design document should be preserved — a new section is appended, not a rewrite.
- **Assumption:** The operator's intent is to consolidate scattered audio guidance into one clear section.
- **Scope creep risk:** The operator may later want to add instructions for other events (e.g., dive bomb, boss sounds) — these should be tracked as separate work items, not added here.

## Related Work

- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** — "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD" (completed)
- **AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE** — "Tank has no audio" (completed)
- **AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19** — "Scout has no audio" (completed)
- **AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ** — "Swarm has no audio" (in progress)
- **AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG** — "Diver has no audio" (in progress)
- **AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU** — "Remove the gap between Scout advance cue and shot" (in progress)

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q:** What scope of audio guidance is expected — per-enemy specifics or general rules?
  - **A (from existing doc):** Both — general rules (spawn/explode owned by base class) and per-enemy specifics (Scout two-phase tell, Tank no-gap pattern, Swarm scene-level volley burst, Diver no audio).
- **Q:** Should this document change any audio implementation code?
  - **A:** No — this is purely a documentation improvement. The audio functions in `src/audio/effects.ts` are out of scope.
data.title: Ensure enemy best practices document include instructions for audio on spawn, shoot and explode.

# Extend power-up catalogue with combat-coupled power-ups

## Summary
Add P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, and P7 Teleport entries to the power-up type catalogue (extending from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT). Each entry includes id, name, icon reference, duration/stack semantics, and a hook identifier for its effect function.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - P3 Shield entry:** Catalogue entry with id `P3`, name `Shield`, duration 15s, single-use (consumed on pop), effect hook `shieldAbsorb`.
- [ ] **AC2 - P4 Bomb entry:** Catalogue entry with id `P4`, name `Bomb`, duration `null` (not timed), single-use, effect hook `bombClear`, with a note that it does not damage enemies per GDD.
- [ ] **AC3 - P6 Phase Shift entry:** Catalogue entry with id `P6`, name `Phase Shift`, duration 3s, single-use (refreshable), effect hook `phaseShift`.
- [ ] **AC4 - P7 Teleport entry:** Catalogue entry with id `P7`, name `Teleport`, stack semantics FIFO (accumulates uses), effect hook `teleport`, with HUD count indicator.
- [ ] **AC5 - Ascending order:** Entries are listed in ascending GDD id order: P3, P4, P6, P7 - matching the round-robin spawn order.
- [ ] **AC6 - No behavioural code:** The catalogue entries are data-only (id, name, icon, duration, stack, hook); no effect implementation lives here.

## Deliverables
- Extended `src/powerups/types.ts` with P3/P4/P6/P7 catalogue entries

## Key Files:
- `src/powerups/types.ts` - add 4 catalogue entries

# Extend effects module with combat-coupled power-up behaviours

## Summary
Extend `src/powerups/effects.ts` (or create it if not yet present from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) with the four combat-coupled effect implementations. Each effect function receives the scene context and ship reference, manages its own state/timer, and exposes an API for the collision pass to query state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - Shield effect (shieldAbsorb):** Returns an effect object with `isActive`, `pop()` method, `apply()` that renders a bubble around the ship, `onHit()` that absorbs one hit and pops, and a timer that expires after 15s. `recollect()` refreshes timer to 15s.
- [ ] **AC2 - Bomb effect (bombClear):** Returns an effect with `apply()` that removes all on-screen enemy bullets (iterates the bullet collection and destroys each), does NOT damage enemy entities. Shows a brief HUD notice string. `recollect()` is a benign no-op.
- [ ] **AC3 - Phase Shift effect (phaseShift):** Returns an effect with `isActive`, `isInvulnerable` flag set to true during active period, `apply()` that renders a ghost outline of the ship, 3s duration timer, `recollect()` refreshes to 3s.
- [ ] **AC4 - Teleport effect (teleport):** Returns an effect with a FIFO stack of remaining uses, `consume()` removes one use and returns true if any remain, `getCount()` returns remaining uses. `apply()` triggers safe-spot resolution (see AC5). On teleport success, grants P6 Phase Shift (3s).
- [ ] **AC5 - Safe-spot resolution (resolveSafeSpot):** A pure function that takes current ship position, travel direction, enemy positions, bullet positions, and safe radius. Returns the nearest safe position along the travel ray (no enemy/bullet within safe radius), clamped to screen bounds. If no safe spot in travel direction, returns nearest on-screen safe position (GDD fallback).
- [ ] **AC6 - Effect factory:** A `createEffect(type, scene, ship)` factory function that dispatches to the correct implementation based on the power-up id.

## Deliverables
- Extended `src/powerups/effects.ts` with shield, bomb, phase shift, teleport, safe-spot, and factory

## Key Files:
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` - add all 4 effect implementations + safe-spot + factory
- `src/core/constants.ts` - reads teleportSafeRadius and flashResetDuration from constants
data.title: Effects module: shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift, teleport

# GymPowerUpsCombat scene - combat-coupled power-up gym

## Summary
Create `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` - a standalone gym scene that demonstrates P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, and P7 Teleport against E1 Scout enemies with shooting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - Scene registration:** Scene key `GymPowerUpsCombat`, label `PowerUps Combat`, registered in the scene loader, auto-discovered by the gym index, listed alongside other gym scenes.
- [ ] **AC2 - Player ship:** Reuses `src/entities/Player.ts` with standard thrust movement + screen-wrap. No auto-fire (weapon power-ups are out of scope).
- [ ] **AC3 - Scout formation:** V-formation of ~6 E1 Scouts (reusing `src/entities/Scout.ts`), with a SHOOT toggle button that enables aimed fire at the ship live position (parameterising the aim target from the fixed demo target).
- [ ] **AC4 - Round-robin spawner:** Spawns P3 to P4 to P6 to P7 in ascending GDD order, one every 5 seconds, each remaining stationary for a 5-second lifetime. Grow from scale 0 to full in 0.5s, shrink to nothing in 0.5s (delta-time driven, matching non-combat gym constants).
- [ ] **AC5 - 3% collection gate:** Drops are only collectible when their current scale > 3% of full size; collection via overlap with ship; uncollected drops fade with no effect.
- [ ] **AC6 - Effect application:** On collection, the corresponding effect from `src/powerups/effects.ts` is applied: P3 to shield bubble, P4 to bullet clear, P6 to phase shift, P7 to teleport (FIFO). Effects render their visuals and manage their own timers.
- [ ] **AC7 - Hit response (AC8):** Collision with an enemy body or enemy bullet, when no P3 shield or P6 phase shift is active, triggers a flash + brief invulnerability + reposition (no lives, no game over). Values from `src/core/constants.ts`.
- [ ] **AC8 - Hit-check suppression:** During P3 active (absorbing) or P6 active (phase shift), hit checks are suppressed - no flash/reset occurs. P3 consumes one absorption on first hit and pops.
- [ ] **AC9 - HUD reuse:** Attaches the standalone HUD class from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) for active-effect icons, names, timers (P3/P6), and counts (P7). No lives counter in this scene.
- [ ] **AC10 - Back button:** Shared `<- INDEX` back button present, navigates to the gym index scene.

## Deliverables
- New `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` scene file
- Parameterised Scout fire target (ship position) - minimal change to `src/entities/Scout.ts` if needed
- HUD attachment in the scene (reusing `src/ui/HUD.ts` unchanged)

## Key Files:
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` - new combat gym scene
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` - parameterise aim target if needed (small change)
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` - reuse unchanged (import only)

# Unit tests for P7 Teleport effect

## Summary
Test the P7 Teleport effect implementation and safe-spot resolution logic in isolation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - FIFO stack semantics:** Each collection pushes to a stack; `consume()` pops the earliest entry and returns true if any remain.
- [ ] **AC2 - Consume depletes stack:** After N consumes for N pickups, `consume()` returns false.
- [ ] **AC3 - Safe-spot resolution avoids enemies:** `resolveSafeSpot()` returns positions free of enemies within the safe radius.
- [ ] **AC4 - Safe-spot resolution avoids bullets:** `resolveSafeSpot()` returns positions free of bullets within the safe radius.
- [ ] **AC5 - Safe spot clamped to screen bounds:** Returned position is always within the screen rectangle.
- [ ] **AC6 - Fallback when no safe spot in travel direction:** Returns nearest on-screen safe position (GDD fallback).
- [ ] **AC7 - Grants P6 Phase Shift on arrival:** On successful teleport, P6 effect is triggered for 3s.

## Key Files:
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` - test file imports and tests teleport + safe-spot
- `src/core/constants.ts` - reads teleport safe radius from constants
data.title: Unit tests: P7 Teleport - FIFO stack, consume, safe-spot resolution

# Unit tests for hit response, collection gate, and spawner

## Summary
Test the hit-response flash/reset, the 3% collection gate, and the round-robin spawn order in isolation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - Flash/reset on hit (no shield/phase shift):** When hit with no active P3/P6, the ship flashes and receives brief invulnerability (from constants).
- [ ] **AC2 - No lives counter on hit:** The flash/reset does not modify a lives counter (no lives model in this scene).
- [ ] **AC3 - No flash/reset during shield active:** When P3 shield is active and absorbing, hit triggers no flash/reset (shield absorbs).
- [ ] **AC4 - No flash/reset during phase shift active:** When P6 phase shift is active, hit triggers no flash/reset.
- [ ] **AC5 - Collection gate at 3%:** Drops below 3% scale are not collected via overlap (returns false).
- [ ] **AC6 - Collection gate above 3%:** Drops above 3% scale ARE collected via overlap (returns true).
- [ ] **AC7 - Round-robin order:** Spawner yields P3, P4, P6, P7 in ascending GDD id order.
- [ ] **AC8 - Spawn cadence:** One power-up every 5 seconds, 5s lifetime.

## Key Files:
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` - test file imports and tests scene helpers
- `src/core/constants.ts` - reads collection threshold and spawn cadence from constants
data.title: Unit tests: hit response, collection gate, round-robin spawner

Discovered while implementing AH-0MTCNZFCD009P5IB (enemy audio best practices doc). The destruction sound ownership rule says the base class GymFormationScene plays playDestructionSound() exactly once per destroyed enemy and entities must NOT call it in their own playExplosion().

Source: src/entities/Phaser.ts playExplosion() calls playDestructionSound() (lines ~162-163), and Phaser.destroySelf() calls playExplosion(). The base class _handleCollisions and explodeRandom() also call playDestructionSound() after destroySelf() — so destroying a Phaser plays the sound twice.

Reference fix already in place for Scout: src/entities/Scout.ts playExplosion() intentionally plays NO sound (design doc §7 no-double-play rule), and src/entities/Scout.test.ts has a no-double-play assertion (expect playDestructionSound not toHaveBeenCalled after destroySelf()).

discovered-from:AH-0MTCNZFCD009P5IB

Acceptance criteria:
1. Destroying a Phaser entity (via EXPLODE and via player-bullet collision) plays playDestructionSound() exactly once.
2. src/entities/Phaser.ts playExplosion() no longer calls playDestructionSound() (or the double-play is otherwise resolved).
3. Existing per-scene tests (GymPhaser.test.ts) pass and a no-double-play assertion mirrors src/entities/Scout.test.ts (entity-level test; expect playDestructionSound not called after destroySelf()).
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
